body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_P(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_1}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=1]-\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_0}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=0]\)

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. Nevertheless, the lower side-mass condition gives positive probability in every one-sided ball around each \(x\in B\), so \(x\) lies in the support of each restricted score law. Sharp assignment and consistency identify the observed conditional regression on side \(t\) with \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere there. The declared Lipschitz representative is continuous; two continuous representatives agreeing almost everywhere on a support agree at every support point, since a nonzero difference would persist on a neighborhood of positive restricted mass. Hence its one-sided limit identifies \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and differencing identifies \(\tau_P(x)\). This identification is setup, not the headline contribution.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine tie-safe membership-pattern representatives, dyadic lower-mass bands, ordered greedy anchors, empirical packing penalties, and one global bandwidth. Second-half outcomes are averaged only at anchors and the clipped contrasts are extended to all boundary points. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is parametrically estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a univariate pointwise minimax order under a regularly varying design density.
The paper studies pointwise smoothness adaptation for an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas L is fixed here.
The paper uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros.
The positive-density random-design supremum benchmark informs the regular endpoint only.
The submanifold-integral result assumes a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.

The positive-density boundary class assumes a continuous density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite moments of order 2+nu; only its conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap is comparable here.

The isotropic boundary result is stated on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary, so its upper theorem does not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class.

body.tldr: A single split-sample estimator now closes the protected global-bandwidth oracle. The first half forms tie-safe membership-pattern representatives, partitions them into dyadic lower-mass bands, builds ordered greedy anchor nets, and selects one global bandwidth; the second half averages only at anchors and extends their clipped contrasts. The conditional maximum is therefore finite and controlled by \(1\vee J_P\), yielding the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) with the same \(\kappa\)-free estimator.

project_justification.gap: Boundary regression with vanishing one-sided mass needs a measurable estimator whose stochastic index set reflects thin-site multiplicity without importing the full continuum of local ball averages.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is a global-bandwidth empirical severity-net oracle over the declared bivariate side-mass class. It combines the tie-safe same-radius packing comparison with an explicit finite anchor extension.
project_justification.fill: Lower-mass bands and ordered greedy anchors give geometrically increasing count scales and anchor cardinalities bounded by the floored empirical packing count. Conditional sub-Gaussian maxima then range only over anchors at one first-half-selected bandwidth, producing an honest \(\inf_h\sup_x\) oracle and simultaneous endpoint upper rates.

body.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies univariate regularly varying designs and pointwise minimax behavior. Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise adaptation over smoothness in an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation, whereas the present Lipschitz constant \(L\) is fixed. Gaiffas (2009) treats univariate designs with finitely many density zeros under spatially normalized loss. Those classes are neither included in nor supersets of the present bivariate side-mass class, so their theorems do not transfer directly. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu assume a continuous score density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments. Only the conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap of that positive-density class is comparable with the regular subcase here; their upper results do not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class. Conversely, estimator-restricted lower bounds remain estimator-restricted. The same-radius comparison and severity-net extension used here are proved directly.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The oracle is deliberately global-bandwidth: its optimization order is \(\inf_h\sup_x\), not the stronger \(\sup_x\inf_h\). The result does not claim arbitrary-profile local-oracle exactness, point-dependent bandwidth adaptation, or exact simultaneous bands beyond the separately declared finite-pattern construction. Constants are uniform only on the compact exponent window bounded away from two.
body.honest_scope: This round proves the pure same-radius empirical-packing lemma, the finite empirical severity-net extension bound, the corrected global-bandwidth population oracle, and simultaneous isolated and pervasive endpoint upper rates. It preserves \(1\vee J_P\) at empty thin sets and handles breakpoint ties, zero second-half counts, empty admissible sets, and \(u=1\). It makes no claim for the discarded pointwise-bandwidth continuum argument and does not infer any arbitrary-profile or local-oracle band guarantee.
body.interpretation: At a fixed bandwidth, the first half learns both empirical severity and how many separated anchors occur at that severity. Assigning each boundary point to a nearby anchor in its own band costs only a constant multiple of \(Lh\). Because the second half evaluates no other centers, the stochastic supremum pays the local floored packing logarithm rather than the number of raw score-induced cells.
